links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Software Engineering Ethics – 1
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Software Engineering Ethics – 1”.

mcqs.question: Choose the correct option in terms of Issues related to professional responsibility

options.c: c) Both Confidentiality & Intellectual property rights

mcqs.answer: c) Both Confidentiality & Intellectual property rights
mcqs.explanation:
Engineers should normally respect the confidentiality of their employers or clients irrespective of whether or not a formal confidentiality agreement has been signed.
They should be aware of local laws governing the use of intellectual property such as patents, copyright, etc.

mcqs.question: “Software engineers should not use their technical skills to misuse other people’s computers.”Here the term misuse refers to:

options.a: a) Unauthorized access to computer material
options.b: b) Unauthorized modification of computer material
options.c: c) Dissemination of viruses or other malware

mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Explain what is meant by PRODUCT with reference to one of the eight principles as per the ACM/IEEE Code of Ethics ?

options.a: a) The product should be easy to use
options.b: b) Software engineers shall ensure that their products and related modifications meet the highest professional standards possible
options.c: c) Software engineers shall ensure that their products and related modifications satisfy the client
options.d: d) It means that the product designed /created should be easily available

mcqs.answer: b) Software engineers shall ensure that their products and related modifications meet the highest professional standards possible
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Identify an ethical dilemma from the situations mentioned below:

options.a: a) Your employer releases a safety-critical system without finishing the testing of the system
options.b: b) Refusing to undertake a project
options.c: c) Agreement in principle with the policies of senior management

mcqs.answer: a) Your employer releases a safety-critical system without finishing the testing of the system
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Identify the correct statement: “Software engineers shall

options.a: a) act in a manner that is in the best interests of his expertise and favour.”
options.b: b) act consistently with the public interest.”
options.c: c) ensure that their products only meet the SRS.”

mcqs.answer: b) act consistently with the public interest.”
mcqs.explanation: Software engineers shall act in a manner that is in the best interests of their client and employer consistent with the public interest and shall ensure that their products and related modifications meet the highest professional standards possible.Thus options a & c are ruled out.

mcqs.question: Select the incorrect statement: “Software engineers should

options.a: a) not knowingly accept work that is outside your competence.”
options.b: b) not use your technical skills to misuse other people’s computers.”
options.c: c) be dependent on their colleagues.”
options.d: d) maintain integrity and independence in their professional judgment.”

mcqs.answer: c) be dependent on their colleagues.”
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Efficiency in a software product does not include ________
mcqs.explanation: Licensing of a software product comes under corporate part of the software company.

mcqs.question: According to an IBM research, “31% of projects are abandoned before they are completed, 53% exceed their cost projections by an average of 189 percent, and 94 projects are restarted for every 100 projects.” What is the significance of these figures?

options.b: b) Lack of software ethics and understanding
options.c: c) Management issues in the company

mcqs.explanation: Lack of software ethics and knowledge, as well as corporate management difficulties, are all aspects of Software Development, therefore this is a possibility. Both are due to a lack of sufficient training.

mcqs.question: The reason for software bugs and failures is due to

options.c: c) Both Software companies and Developers

mcqs.answer: c) Both Software companies and Developers
mcqs.explanation: Software companies are responsible for making policies and providing working atmosphere for the software development, so in turn these companies become a part of software development process.Bugs from developers side is no new thing. Thus option c answers the question.

mcqs.question: Company has latest computers and state-of the- art software tools, so we shouldn’t worry about the quality of the product.
mcqs.explanation: The infrastructure is only one of the several factors that determine the quality of the product.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Software Engineering Ethics – 2
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Software Engineering Ethics – 2”.

mcqs.question: Which of these are not among the eight principles followed by Software Engineering Code of Ethics and Professional Practice ?
mcqs.explanation: Rest all are clauses for software ethics, environment does not focus on specific clause nor its of importace related to question.

mcqs.question: What is a Software ?

options.a: a) Software is set of programs
options.b: b) Software is documentation and configuration of data
options.c: c) Software is set of programs, documentation & configuration of data

mcqs.answer: c) Software is set of programs, documentation & configuration of data
mcqs.explanation: Software is not just set of program but it is also associated documentation and configuration of data to make program run.

mcqs.question: Which of these does not account for software failure ?
mcqs.explanation: Increasing supply will lead to more production and not failure.

mcqs.question: What are attributes of good software ?
mcqs.explanation: Good software should deliver the required functinality, maintainability. Software development is not an attribute but a fundamental.

mcqs.question: Which of these software engineering activities are not a part of software processes ?
mcqs.explanation: Software dependence is an attribute and not an engineering activity for process.

mcqs.question: Which of these is incorrect ?

options.a: a) Software engineering belongs to Computer science
options.b: b) Software engineering is a part of more general form of System Engineering
options.c: c) Computer science belongs to Software engineering
options.d: d) Software engineering is concerned with the practicalities of developing  and delivering useful software

mcqs.answer: c) Computer science belongs to Software engineering
mcqs.explanation: Software engineering is a vast sub domain which comes under computer science which is main domain.

mcqs.question: Which of these is true ?

options.a: a) Generic products and customized products are types of software products
options.b: b) Generic products are produced by organization and sold to open market
options.c: c) Customized products are commissioned by particular customer

mcqs.explanation: All of them are true.

mcqs.question: Which of these does not affect different types of software  as a whole?
mcqs.explanation: Option b & c are a part of Software Engineering as a subject,hence option a covers them both.

mcqs.question: The fundamental notions of software engineering does not account for ?
mcqs.explanation: Software validation is an activity for software process and not the fundamental for engineering.

mcqs.question: Which of these is not true ?

options.a: a) Web has led to availability of software services and possibility of developing highly distributed service based systems
options.b: b) Web based systems have led to degradation of programming languages
options.c: c) Web brings concept of software as service
options.d: d) Web based system should be developed and delivered incrementally

mcqs.answer: b) Web based systems have led to degradation of programming languages
mcqs.explanation: Web based systems has led to important advances in programming languages.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Software Life Cycle Models
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Software Life Cycle Models”.

mcqs.question: Build & Fix Model is suitable for programming exercises of ___________ LOC (Line of Code).
mcqs.explanation: Build & Fix Model is suitable for small projects & programming exercises of 100 or 200 lines.

mcqs.question: RAD stands for
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following models is not suitable for accommodating any change?
mcqs.explanation: Real projects rarely follow the sequential flow that the Waterfall Model proposes.

mcqs.question: Which is not one of the types of prototype of Prototyping Model?
mcqs.explanation: Their is no such thing as Diagonal Prototype whereas other options have their respective definitions.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not a phase of Prototyping Model?
mcqs.explanation: A prototyping model generates only a working model of a system.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements regarding Build & Fix Model is wrong?

options.a: a) No room for structured design
options.b: b) Code soon becomes unfixable & unchangeable
options.c: c) Maintenance is practically not possible
options.d: d) It scales up well to large projects

mcqs.answer: d) It scales up well to large projects
mcqs.explanation: Build & Fix Model is suitable for 100-200 LOC

mcqs.question: RAD Model has
mcqs.explanation: RAD Model consists of five phases namely:Business modeling,Data modeling,Process modeling,Application generation and Testing & Turnover.

mcqs.question: What is the major drawback of using RAD Model?

options.a: a) Highly specialized & skilled developers/designers are required
options.d: d) Increases reusability of components, Highly specialized & skilled developers/designers are required

mcqs.answer: d) Increases reusability of components, Highly specialized & skilled developers/designers are required
mcqs.explanation: The client may create an unrealistic product vision leading a team to over or under-develop functionality.Also, the specialized & skilled developers are not easily available.

mcqs.question: SDLC stands for
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Which model can be selected if user is involved in all the phases of SDLC?

options.d: d) both Prototyping Model & RAD Model

mcqs.explanation: None.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Evolutionary Software Process Models
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Evolutionary Software Process Models”.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not an Evolutionary Process Model?
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: The Incremental Model is a result of combination of elements of which two models?

options.a: a) Build & FIX Model & Waterfall Model

mcqs.explanation: Each linear sequence produces a deliverable “increment” of the software and particularly when we have to quickly deliver a limited functionality system.

mcqs.question: What is the major advantage of using Incremental Model?

options.a: a) Customer can respond to each increment
options.b: b) Easier to test and debug
options.c: c) It is used when there is a need to get a product to the market early
options.d: d) Easier to test and debug & It is used when there is a need to get a product to the market early

mcqs.answer: d) Easier to test and debug & It is used when there is a need to get a product to the market early
mcqs.explanation: Incremental Model is generally easier to test and debug than other methods of software development because relatively smaller changes are made during each iteration and is popular particularly when we have to quickly deliver a limited functionality system.However, option “a” can be seen in other models as well like RAD model,hence option “d” answers the question.

mcqs.question: The spiral model was originally proposed by
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: The spiral model has two dimensions namely _____________ and ____________
mcqs.explanation: The radial dimension of the model represents the cumulative costs and the angular dimension represents the progress made in completing each cycle. Each loop of the spiral from X-axis clockwise through 360<sup>o</sup> represents one phase.

mcqs.question: How is WINWIN Spiral Model different from Spiral Model?

options.a: a) It defines tasks required to define resources, timelines, and other project related information
options.b: b) It defines a set of negotiation activities at the beginning of each pass around the spiral
options.c: c) It defines tasks required to assess both technical and management risks
options.d: d) It defines tasks required to construct, test, install, and provide user support

mcqs.answer: b) It defines a set of negotiation activities at the beginning of each pass around the spiral
mcqs.explanation: Except option “b” all other tasks/activities are present in Spiral Model as well.

mcqs.question: Identify the disadvantage of Spiral Model.

options.a: a) Doesn’t work well for smaller projects
options.b: b) High amount of risk analysis
options.c: c) Strong approval and documentation control
options.d: d) Additional Functionality can be added at a later date

mcqs.answer: a) Doesn’t work well for smaller projects
mcqs.explanation: All other options are the advantages of Spiral Model.

mcqs.question: Spiral Model has user involvement in all its phases.
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: How is Incremental Model different from Spiral Model?

options.a: a) Progress can be measured for Incremental Model
options.b: b) Changing requirements can be accommodated in Incremental Model
options.c: c) Users can see the system early in Incremental Model

mcqs.answer: a) Progress can be measured for Incremental Model
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: If you were to create client/server applications, which model would you go for?
mcqs.explanation: When applied to client/server applications, the concurrent process model defines activities in two dimensions: a system dimension and a component dimension.Thus Concurrency is achieved by system and component activities occurring simultaneously and can be modeled using the state-oriented approach.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Selection of a Life Cycle Model
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Selection of a Life Cycle Model”.

mcqs.question: Selection of a model is based on

options.c: c) Project type and associated risk

mcqs.explanation: Each model has to have some requirements, a team of developers, users and the risk involved in developing a project.

mcqs.question: Which two models doesn’t allow defining requirements early in the cycle?
mcqs.explanation: Prototyping Model starts with a requirements analysis phase including techniques like FAST, QFD, Brainstorming.In case of Spiral model the first phase involves activities related to customer communication like determining objectives.

mcqs.question: Which of the following life cycle model can be chosen if the development team has less experience on similar projects?
mcqs.explanation: Relying on risk assessment/analysis provides more flexibility than required for many applications which overcomes the criteria of less experienced developers.

mcqs.question: If you were a lead developer of a software company and you are asked to submit a project/product within a stipulated time-frame with no cost barriers, which model would you select?
mcqs.explanation: RAD model is inapplicable to develop cheaper products/software/projects as the cost of modeling, hiring highly skilled developers/designers and automated code generation is very high.But here the cost is not an issue, so one can select this model as it reduces development time.

mcqs.question: Which two of the following models will not be able to give the desired outcome if user’s participation is not involved?
mcqs.explanation: Active Participation of user is involved in all the four phases of RAD model and in case of the Prototyping model we need user’s presence/involvement every time a new prototype is build or designed.

mcqs.question: A company is developing an advance version of their current software available in the market, what model approach would they prefer ?
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: One can choose Waterfall Model if the project development schedule is tight.
mcqs.explanation: Real projects rarely follow the sequential flow and iterations in this model are handled indirectly. This changes can cause confusion as the project proceeds thereby delaying the delivery date.

mcqs.question: Choose the correct option from given below:

options.a: a) Prototyping Model facilitates reusability of components
options.b: b) RAD Model Model facilitates reusability of components
options.c: c) Both RAD & Prototyping Model facilitates reusability of components

mcqs.answer: c) Both RAD & Prototyping Model facilitates reusability of components
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Spiral Model has high reliability requirements.
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: RAD Model has high reliability requirements.
mcqs.explanation: None.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Fourth Generation Techniques
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Fourth Generation Techniques”.

mcqs.question: Identify a fourth generation language(4GL) from the given below.
mcqs.explanation: Rest all are third generation languages(3GL).

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following activities for making a software product using 4GT. i. Design strategy
ii. Transformation into product
iii. Implementation
iv. Requirement gathering
mcqs.explanation: The sequence of activities mentioned in option c represents the Fourth Generation Techniques(4GT)Model.

mcqs.question: 4GL is an example of ______________ processing.
mcqs.explanation: Functional processing/testing is also referred to as black box testing in which contents of the black box are not known.Almost anything might be referred to as a black box:an algorithm or the human mind.Functionality of the black box is understood in terms of its inputs and outputs.

mcqs.question: The 4GT Model is a package of ______________
mcqs.explanation: 4GT encompasses a broad array of software tools enabling the software engineer to specify the characteristics at a high level leading to an automatically generated source code based on these specifications.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a type of a 4GL? One originating ______________
mcqs.explanation: Fifth-generation programming language are built on LISP.

mcqs.question: In 4GT, we can specify the user requirements in graphic notation or small abbreviated language form.
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Productivity of software engineers is reduced in using a 4GT.
mcqs.explanation: 4GLs are more programmer-friendly and enhance programming efficiency with usage of English-like words and phrases, thereby increasing the productivity of professionals able to engage in software development.

mcqs.question: Which of the following 4GLs invented at IBM and subsequently adopted by ANSI and ISO as the standard language for managing structured data?
mcqs.explanation: C & JAVA are third generation languages(3GLs) whereas PROLOG is a 5GL.

mcqs.question: What is a major advantage of using a 4GT Model for producing small scale products, applications or programs ?

options.a: a) Improved productivity of software engineers
options.b: b) Reduction in software development time
options.c: c) 4GT helped by CASE tools and code generators offers a credible solution to many software problems

mcqs.answer: b) Reduction in software development time
mcqs.explanation: Since automated coding is done using CASE tools & code generators proponents claim a dramatic reduction in software development time.

mcqs.question: Which of the following model has a major disadvantage in terms of the coding phase of a software life cycle model ?
mcqs.explanation: Since coding phase is eliminated in 4GT Model,more expertise is required for analysis,design and testing activities.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Software Process and Product – 1
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Software Process and Product – 1”.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not a software process quality?
mcqs.explanation: Portability is a software product quality which means software can run on different hardware platforms or software environments.

mcqs.question: _____________&_____________ are two kinds of software products.
mcqs.explanation: rest all are sub categories/applications of option c.

mcqs.question: Software costs more to maintain than it does to develop.
mcqs.explanation: For systems with a long life, maintenance costs may be several times development costs.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not an application of embedded software product?

options.a: a) keypad control of a security system
options.c: c) digital function of dashboard display in a car

mcqs.explanation: Pattern recognition uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) software.

mcqs.question: Purpose of process is to deliver software

options.d: d) both in time & with acceptable quality

mcqs.answer: d) both in time & with acceptable quality
mcqs.explanation: Cost of a software is a management issue & is not related to process activities.

mcqs.question:
The work associated with software engineering can be categorized into three generic phases,regardless of application area, project size, or complexity namely the__________ phase which focuses on what, the_________ phase which focuses on how and the_________ phase which focuses on change. i. support
ii. development
iii. definition
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Which of the following activities of a Generic Process framework provides a feedback report?
mcqs.explanation: In Deployment the product is delivered to the customer who evaluates the product and provides feedback based on the evaluation.

mcqs.question: Process adopted for one project is same as the process adopted from another project.
mcqs.explanation: the overall flow of activities, actions,tasks,the level of autonomy given to the software team and the inter dependencies among two process can never be the same.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not an Umbrella Activity that complements the five process framework activities and help team manage and control progress, quality, change, and risk.
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Four types of change are encountered during the support phase.Which one of the following is not one that falls into such category?
mcqs.explanation: Translation is done in the development phase.

links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Software Process and Product – 2”.

mcqs.question: If a software production gets behind schedule, one can add more programmers and catch up.
mcqs.explanation: As new people are added, people who were working must spend time educating the newcomers, thereby reducing the amount of time spent on productive development effort.

mcqs.question: Choose an internal software quality from given below:

mcqs.question: RUP stands for____________ created by a division of ____________

options.a: a) It shows the process activities that are enacted

mcqs.question: The only deliverable work product for a successful project is the working program.
mcqs.explanation: A working program is only one part of a software configuration that includes many elements. Documentation provides a foundation for successful engineering and, more important, guidance for software support.

mcqs.question: Which phase of the RUP is used to establish a business case for the system ?
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not a fundamental activity for software processes in software engineering ?
mcqs.explanation: Software Verification is accounted for in implementation & testing activity.

mcqs.question: A general statement of objectives is the major cause of failed software efforts.
mcqs.explanation: A formal and detailed description of the information domain, function, behavior, performance, interfaces, design constraints and validation criteria is essential which can be determined only after thorough communication between customer and developer.

mcqs.question: The longer a fault exists in software

options.a: a) the more tedious its removal becomes
options.b: b) the more costly it is to detect and correct
options.c: c) the less likely it is to be properly corrected

mcqs.question: Component-based Software Engineering allows faster delivery.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the following steps to form a basic/general Engineering Process Model. i. Test
ii. Design

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Agile Software Development
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Agile Software Development”.

mcqs.question: Select the option that suits the Manifesto for Agile Software Development
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Agile Software Development is based on

options.d: d) Both Incremental and Iterative Development

mcqs.answer: d) Both Incremental and Iterative Development
mcqs.explanation: The software is developed in increments with the customer specifying the requirements to be included in each increment and the highest priority is to satisfy the customer through early and continuous delivery of valuable software. They are iterative because they work on one iteration followed by improvements in next iteration

mcqs.question: Which on of the following is not an agile method?
mcqs.explanation: The 4GT approach does not incorporate iteration and the continuous feedback,which is the fundamental aspect of an agile method.

mcqs.question: Agility is defined as the ability of a project team to respond rapidly to a change.
mcqs.explanation: The aim of agile methods is to reduce overheads in the software process and to be able to respond quickly to changing requirements without excessive rework.

mcqs.question: How is plan driven development different from agile development ?

options.a: a) Outputs are decided through a process of negotiation during the software development process
options.b: b) Specification, design, implementation and testing are interleaved

mcqs.explanation: A plan-driven approach to software engineering is based around separate development stages with the outputs to be produced at each of these stages planned in advance.

mcqs.question: How many phases are there in Scrum ?

options.d: d) Scrum is an agile method which means it does not have phases

mcqs.explanation: There are three phases in Scrum.The initial phase is an outline planning phase followed by a series of sprint cycles and project closure phase.

mcqs.question: Agile methods seem to work best when team members have a relatively high skill level.
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: Which of the following does not apply to agility to a software process?

options.a: a) Uses incremental product delivery strategy
options.b: b) Only essential work products are produced
options.c: c) Eliminate the use of project planning and testing

mcqs.answer: c) Eliminate the use of project planning and testing
mcqs.explanation: Testing is a major part of each software development process which can’t be avoided.

mcqs.question: Which three framework activities are present in Adaptive Software Development(ASD) ?

options.b: b) requirements gathering, adaptive cycle planning, iterative development

mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: In agile development it is more important to build software that meets the customers’ needs today than worry about features that might be needed in the future.
mcqs.explanation: None.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Extreme Programming
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Extreme Programming”.

mcqs.question: Incremental development in Extreme Programming (XP) is supported through a system release once every month.
mcqs.explanation: Incremental development is supported through small, frequent system releases.

mcqs.question: In XP, as soon as the work on a task is complete, it is integrated into the whole system.
mcqs.explanation: XP follows a continuous integration approach.After any such integration, all the unit tests in the system must pass.

mcqs.question: In XP Increments are delivered to customers every _______ weeks.
mcqs.explanation: Extreme Programming (XP) takes an ‘extreme’ approach to iterative development.New versions may be built several times per day, hence delivering the increment for approval every 2nd week after testing the new version.

mcqs.question: User requirements are expressed as __________ in Extreme Programming.
mcqs.explanation: User requirements are expressed as scenarios or user stories.These are written on cards and the development team break them down into implementation tasks. These tasks are the basis of schedule and cost estimates.

mcqs.question: Is a customer involved test development and validation in XP ?

options.c: c) It may vary from Customer to Customer

mcqs.answer: c) It may vary from Customer to Customer
mcqs.explanation: The role of the customer in the testing process is to help develop acceptance tests for the stories that are to be implemented in the next release of the system.However, people adopting the customer role have limited time available and so cannot work full-time with the development team. They may feel that providing the requirements was enough of a contribution and so may be reluctant to get involved in the testing process.

mcqs.question: Programmers prefer programming to testing and sometimes they take shortcuts when writing tests. For example, they may write incomplete tests that do not check for all possible exceptions that may occur.
mcqs.explanation: In XP Some tests can be very difficult to write incrementally.For example, in a complex user interface, it is often difficult to write unit tests for the code that implements the ‘display logic’ and workflow between screens.

mcqs.question: Tests are automated in Extreme Programming.
mcqs.explanation: Automated test harnesses are used to run all component tests each time that a new release is built.

mcqs.question: In XP an automated unit test framework is used to write tests for a new piece of functionality before that functionality itself is implemented.
mcqs.explanation: XP follows Test-first development approach.

mcqs.question: Developers work individually on a release and they compare their results with other developers before forwarding that release to customers.
mcqs.explanation: XP follows the principle of pair programming which means developers work in pairs, checking each other’s work and providing the support to always do a good job.

mcqs.question: Which four framework activities are found in the Extreme Programming(XP) ?
mcqs.explanation: XP involves the mentioned four activities, and in the same in order.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Requirement Engineering
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Requirement Engineering”.

mcqs.question: What are the types of requirements ?
mcqs.explanation: All the mentioned traits are beneficial for an effective product to be developed.

mcqs.question: Select the developer-specific requirement ?
mcqs.explanation: Availability is user specific requirement.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not a step of requirement engineering?
mcqs.explanation: Requirement Elicitation, Requirement Analysis, Requirement Documentation and Requirement Review are the four crucial process steps of requirement engineering.Design is in itself a different phase of Software Engineering.

mcqs.question: FAST stands for
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: QFD stands for
mcqs.explanation: None.

mcqs.question: A Use-case actor is always a person having a role that different people may play.
mcqs.explanation: Use-case Actor is anything that needs to interact with the system, be it a person or another (external) system.

mcqs.question: The user system requirements are the parts of which document ?
mcqs.explanation: Software requirements specification (SRS), is a complete description of the behaviour of a system to be developed and may include a set of use cases that describe interactions the users will have with the software.

mcqs.question: A stakeholder is anyone who will purchase the completed software system under development.
mcqs.explanation: Stakeholders are anyone who has an interest in the project. Project stakeholders are individuals and organizations that are actively involved in the project, or whose interests may be affected as a result of project execution or project completion.

mcqs.question: Conflicting requirements are common in Requirement Engineering, with each client proposing  his or her version is the right one.
mcqs.explanation: This situation is seen in every field of work as each professional has his/her way of looking onto things & would argue to get his/her point approved.

mcqs.question: Which is one of the most important stakeholder from the following ?
mcqs.explanation: Users are always the most important stakeholders.After all, without users or customers, what’s the point of being in business?.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Functional and Non-Functional Requirements
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Functional and Non-Functional Requirements”.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is a functional requirement ?
mcqs.explanation: All are non-functional requirements representing quality of the system. Functional requirements describe what the software has to do.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is a requirement that fits in a developer’s module ?
mcqs.explanation: A developer needs to test his product before launching it into the market.

mcqs.question: “Consider a system where, a heat sensor detects an intrusion and alerts the security company.” What kind of a requirement the system is providing ?
mcqs.explanation: Functional requirements describe what the software has to do.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements explains portability in non-functional requirements?

options.a: a) It is a degree to which software running on one platform can easily be converted to run on another platform
options.b: b) It cannot be enhanced by using languages, OS’ and tools that are universally available and standardized
options.c: c) The ability of the system to behave consistently in a user-acceptable manner when operating within the environment for which the system was intended

mcqs.answer: a) It is a degree to which software running on one platform can easily be converted to run on another platform
mcqs.explanation: Option c is termed as reliability and option e refers to efficiency.

mcqs.question: Functional requirements capture the intended behavior of the system.
mcqs.explanation: The behavior of functional requirements may be expressed as services, tasks or functions the system is required to perform.

mcqs.question: Choose the incorrect statement with respect to Non-Functional Requirement(NFR).

options.a: a) Product-oriented Approach – Focus on system (or software) quality
options.b: b) Process-oriented Approach – Focus on how NFRs can be used in the design process
options.c: c) Quantitative Approach – Find measurable scales for the functionality attributes
options.d: d) Qualitative Approach – Study various relationships between quality goals

mcqs.answer: c) Quantitative Approach – Find measurable scales for the functionality attributes
mcqs.explanation: Quantitative Approaches in NFRs are used to find measurable scales for the quality attributes like efficiency, flexibility, integrity, usability etc.

mcqs.question: How many classification schemes have been developed for NFRs ?
mcqs.explanation:
Software Quality Tree [Boehm 1976], Roman [IEEE Computer 1985], Process-Product-External considerations [Sommerville 1992], Mc Call’s NFR list and Dimensions of Quality–Components of FURPS+ are the five classification schemes for NFRs.
.

mcqs.question: According to components of FURPS+, which of the following does not belong to S ?
mcqs.explanation: Speed Efficiency belong to Performance (P) in FURPS+ .

mcqs.question: Does software wear & tear by decomposition ?
mcqs.explanation: Unlike hardware, software is reliable.

mcqs.question: What are the four dimensions of Dependability ?
mcqs.explanation: All the traits of option c sync with dependability.

mcqs.question: Choose the correct statement on how NFRs integrates with Rational Unified Process ?

options.a: a) System responds within 4 seconds on average to local user requests and changes in the environment
options.b: b) System responds within 4 seconds on average to remote user requests and changes in the environment

mcqs.answer: b) System responds within 4 seconds on average to remote user requests and changes in the environment
mcqs.explanation: System response to a local user is 2 seconds on average.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Requirement Elicitation
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Requirement Elicitation”.

mcqs.question: What is the first step of requirement elicitation ?
mcqs.explanation: Stakeholders are the one who will invest in and use the product, so its essential to chalk out stakeholders first.

mcqs.question:
Starting from least to most important, choose the order of stakeholder. i. Managers
ii. Entry level Personnel
iii. Users
iv. Middle level stakeholder
mcqs.explanation: Users are your customers, they will be using your product, thus making them most important of all.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the tasks involved in requirements elicitation in an appropriate manner. i. Consolidation
ii. Prioritization
iii. Requirements Gathering
iv. Evaluation
mcqs.explanation: Requirements gathering captures viewpoint from different users followed by evaluation of those view points.Now comes the task of checking the relative importance of the requirements and finally to consolidate or bind together the information collected.

mcqs.question: What are the types of requirement in Quality Function Deployment(QFD) ?
mcqs.explanation: According to QFD, Normal, Expected and Exciting requirements maximizes customer satisfaction from the Software Engineering Process.

mcqs.question: What kind of approach was introduced for elicitation and modelling to give a functional view of the system ?
mcqs.explanation: Use Case captures who does what with the system, for what purpose, without dealing with system internals.

mcqs.question: What are the kinds of actors used in OOSE ?
mcqs.explanation: A primary actor is one having a goal requiring the assistance of the system whereas, a secondary actor is one from which system needs assistance.There is no such thing as ternary actor in Software Engineering.

mcqs.question: Why is Requirements Elicitation a difficult task ?
mcqs.explanation: Users specify unnecessary technical detail that may confuse, rather than clarify overall system objectives.Also, the customers/users are not completely sure of what is needed, have a poor understanding of the capabilities and limitations of their computing environment and they do not understand that the requirements change over time.

mcqs.question: What requirement gathering method developed at IBM in 1970s is used for managing requirement elicitation ?
mcqs.explanation: Joint application design (JAD) is a process used to collect business requirements while developing new information systems for a company. Requirements traceability is concerned with documenting the life of a requirement and providing bi-directional traceability between various associated requirements.

mcqs.question: Requirements elicitation is a cyclic process
mcqs.explanation: Requirements traceability provides bi-directional traceability between various associated requirements.

mcqs.question: How many Scenarios are there in elicitation activities ?
mcqs.explanation: As-is Scenario, Visionary Scenario, Evaluation Scenario and Training Scenario are the four scenarios in requirement elicitation activities.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Requirement Elicitation Techniques – 1
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Requirement Elicitation Techniques -1”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following elicitation techniques is a viewpoint based method?
mcqs.explanation: Controlled Requirements Expression(CORE) says that any system can be viewed from a number of view points and that a complete picture of system requirements can only emerge by putting together the various viewpoints.

mcqs.question: ___________ and ____________ are the two view points discussed in Controlled Requirements Expression (CORE).
mcqs.explanation: The CORE sessions includes the discussion of functional and non-functional requirements.

mcqs.question: What is the major drawback of CORE ?

options.b: b) NFRs are not given enough importance
options.c: c) Role of analyst is passive

mcqs.answer: c) Role of analyst is passive
mcqs.explanation: In CORE the requirement specification are put together by all users, customers and analysts, so a passive analyst will not get the requirements properly.

mcqs.question: Choose a framework that corresponds to Issue Based Information System (IBIS).

options.d: d) Both Question -> Idea -> Argument and Issue -> Position -> Justification

mcqs.answer: d) Both Question -> Idea -> Argument and Issue -> Position -> Justification
mcqs.explanation: IBIS is a simple and non-intrusive method that provides a framework for  resolving issues and gathering requirements.

mcqs.question: How is CORE different from IBIS ?

options.c: c) It is simple and an easier method to use
options.d: d) Consistency problems are addressed in CORE

mcqs.answer: d) Consistency problems are addressed in CORE
mcqs.explanation: Preliminary data collection is done in CORE to get some broad level data on each view point to structure the view point and to check consistency from within and outside the viewpoints.

mcqs.question: Which of the following Requirement Elicitation Techniques removes the poor understanding of application domain and lack of common terminology between the users and the analysts ?
mcqs.explanation: Feature Oriented Domain Analysis (FODA) is defined as the process of identifying, collecting, organizing and representing relevant information in a domain .

mcqs.question: How many steps are involved in Feature Oriented Domain Analysis (FODA) ?
mcqs.explanation: Context Analysis, Domain Modeling and Architecture Modeling are the three steps involved in Feature Oriented Domain Analysis (FODA).

mcqs.question: IBIS is a more structured approach than CORE.
mcqs.explanation: IBIS is a more structured approach as it captures information which is consistent and important.On the other hand CORE gives importance to every view point even if it is obsolete.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is not an actor in JAD sessions ?
mcqs.explanation: A Tester’s role is seen in after coding phase rather than in elicitation phase.

mcqs.question: What of the following is not an output of a JAD session ?
mcqs.explanation: Unified Modeling Language (UML) diagrams are constructed during the design phase of the SDLC.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Requirement Elicitation Techniques – 2
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Requirement Elicitation Techniques – 2”.

mcqs.question: How is brainstorming different from JAD ? Brainstorming sessions

options.c: c) cover the technology used for the development

mcqs.explanation: Brainstorming is a group or individual creativity technique by which efforts are made to find a conclusion for a specific problem by gathering a list of ideas spontaneously contributed by its member(s).The idea is to quickly reach to an approved solution ASAP.

mcqs.question: How is throwaway prototype different from evolutionary prototype ?

options.b: b) It involves just one task
options.c: c) The prototype is built with the idea that it will eventually be converted into final system
options.d: d) It has a shorter development time

mcqs.answer: b) It involves just one task
mcqs.explanation: Except option b all other options represent the characteristics of an evolutionary prototype.

mcqs.question: Keeping the requirements of QFD in mind which of the following is not an example of an Expected Requirement ?

options.b: b) Overall operational correctness and reliability

mcqs.explanation: Expected requirements are so fundamental that a customer does not explicitly state them.System functions comes under the category of Normal requirements in QFD which is compulsory to be defined,hence is not an expected requirement.

mcqs.question: QFD works best if it has management commitment.
mcqs.explanation: QFD involves heavy investment in initial stages, thus bounding the management to provide appropriate funding for the development process .

mcqs.question: Which of the following Requirement Elicitation Techniques is applicable to messy, changing and ill-defined problem situations ?
mcqs.explanation: Soft systems methodology (SSM) is a systemic approach for tackling real-world problematic situations.It is a common misunderstanding that SSM is a methodology for dealing solely with ‘soft problems’ (problems which involve psychological, social, and cultural elements). SSM does not differentiate between ‘soft’ and ‘hard’ problems, it merely provides a different way of dealing with situations perceived as problematic.

mcqs.question: To ensure that a given root definition is rigorous and comprehensive, The Lancaster team proposed several criteria that are summarized in the mnemonic CATWOE in Soft Systems Methodology (SSM).Which of the following alphabet is representing an entirely different meaning to SSM ?
mcqs.explanation: ‘E’ in CATWOE stands for Environmental constraints.

mcqs.question: Choose the disadvantage of using SSM as an elicitation technique.

options.a: a) It incorporates human element into design
options.b: b) SSM is in its infant stage
options.c: c) SSM is suitable for new systems
options.d: d) Standard methodologies like Role Exploration, Issue Resolution and Reorganization support SSM

mcqs.answer: b) SSM is in its infant stage
mcqs.explanation: SSM is still in its infancy.It is evolving and its industrial usage is low.

mcqs.question: How many phases are there in Brainstorming ?
mcqs.explanation: Preparation, Execution and Follow up are the three phases to be achieved for a successful brainstorming session.

mcqs.question: Who controls the FAST (Facilitated Application Specification Techniques) meeting ?
mcqs.explanation: A Facilitator (a customer/developer/an outsider) controls the FAST meeting.His role is to ensure that the meeting is productive.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the steps in order to represent the conducting of Wideband Delphi Technique. i. Conduct a group discussion
ii. Conduct another group discussion
iii. Present experts with a problem
iv. Collect expert opinion anonymously
v. Iterate until consensus is reached
vi. Feedback a summary of result to each expert

options.a: a) i, iii, ii, iv, v, vi
options.b: b) iii, i, ii, iv, v, vi
options.c: c) i, ii, iii, iv, vi, v
options.d: d) iii, i, iv, vi, ii, v

mcqs.answer: d) iii, i, iv, vi, ii, v
mcqs.explanation: The sequence represents the working steps of a Wideband Delphi technique .

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Requirement Analysis
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Requirement Analysis”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a diagram studied in Requirement Analysis ?
mcqs.explanation: Activity Diagram comes under the design phase of SDLC.

mcqs.question: How many feasibility studies is conducted in Requirement Analysis ?
mcqs.explanation: Economic feasibility (cost/benefit analysis), Technical feasibility (hardware/software/people, etc.) and Legal feasibility studies are done in Requirement Analysis.

mcqs.question: How many phases are there in Requirement Analysis ?
mcqs.explanation: Problem Recognition, Evaluation and Synthesis (focus is on what not how), Modeling, Specification and Review are the  five phases.

mcqs.question: Traceability is not considered in Requirement Analysis.
mcqs.explanation: Requirements traceability is concerned with documenting the life of a requirement and providing bi-directional traceability between various associated requirements, hence requirements must be traceable.

mcqs.question: Requirements analysis is critical to the success of a development project.

options.c: c) Depends upon the size of project

mcqs.explanation: Requirements must be actionable, measurable, testable, related to identified business needs or opportunities, and defined to a level of detail sufficient for system design.

mcqs.question: _________ and _________ are the two issues of Requirement Analysis.
mcqs.explanation: Option a and c are the types of requirements and not the issues of requirement analysis..

mcqs.question: The requirements that result from requirements analysis are typically expressed from one of three perspectives or views.WhaT is that perspective or view ?
mcqs.explanation: The perspectives or views have been described as the Operational, Functional, and Physical views.All three are necessary and must be coordinated to fully understand the customers’ needs and objectives.

mcqs.question: Requirements Analysis is an Iterative Process.
mcqs.explanation: Requirements analysis is conducted iteratively with functional analysis to optimize performance requirements for identified functions, and to verify that synthesized solutions can satisfy customer requirements.

mcqs.question: Coad and Yourdon suggested _______ selection characteristics that should be used as an analyst considers each potential object for inclusion in the requirement analysis model.
mcqs.explanation: Retained information, Needed services, Multiple attributes, Common attributes, Common operations and Essential requirements are the six criterion mentioned by Coad and Yourdon.

mcqs.question: Requirements should specify ‘what’ but not ‘how’.
mcqs.explanation: ‘What’ refers to a system’s purpose, while ‘How’ refers to a system’s structure and behavior.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Requirement Documentation
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Requirement Documentation”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following property does not correspond to a good Software Requirements Specification (SRS) ?
mcqs.explanation: The SRS should be unambiguous in nature which means each sentence in SRS should have a unique interpretation.

mcqs.question: Which of the following property of SRS is depicted by the statement : “Conformity to a standard is maintained” ?
mcqs.explanation: The SRS is complete full labeling and referencing of all figures, tables etc. and definition of all terms and units of measure is defined.

mcqs.question: The SRS is said to be consistent if and only if

options.a: a) its structure and style are such that any changes to the requirements can be made easily while retaining the style and structure
options.b: b) every requirement stated therein is one that the software shall meet
options.c: c) every requirement stated therein is verifiable
options.d: d) no subset of individual requirements described in it conflict with each other

mcqs.answer: d) no subset of individual requirements described in it conflict with each other
mcqs.explanation: Real world object may conflict with each other for example one requirement says that all lights should be red while the other states that all lights should green.

mcqs.question:
Which of the following statements about SRS is/are true ? i. SRS is written by customer
ii. SRS is written by a developer
iii. SRS serves as a contract between customer and developer

options.b: b) Both ii and iii are true

mcqs.explanation: The SRS acts as a communication media between the Customer, Analyst, system developers, maintainers etc. Thus it is a contract between Purchaser and Supplier. It is essentially written by a developer on the basis of customer’ need but in some cases it may be written by a customer as well.

mcqs.question: The SRS document is also known as _____________ specification.
mcqs.explanation: The system is considered as a black box whose internal details are not known that is, only its visible external (input/output) behavior is documented.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is included in SRS ?
mcqs.explanation: Design constraints include standards to be incorporated in the software, implementation language, resource limits, operating environment etc.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not included in SRS ?
mcqs.explanation: The SRS document concentrates on:”what needs to be done” and carefully avoids the solution (“how to do”) aspects.

mcqs.question:
Arrange the given sequence to form a SRS Prototype outline as per IEEE SRS Standard. i. General description
ii. Introduction
iii. Index
iv. Appendices
v. Specific Requirements

options.b: b) iii, ii, i, v, iv
options.c: c) ii, i, v, iv, iii

mcqs.answer: c) ii, i, v, iv, iii
mcqs.explanation: The given sequence correctly resemble a standard SRS prototype as per IEEE.

mcqs.question: Consider the following Statement: “The output of a program shall be given within 10 secs of event X 10% of the time.”What characteristic of SRS is being depicted here ?
mcqs.explanation: An SRS is verifiable, if and only if, every requirement stated therein is verifiable.Here the given condition can be verified during testing phase.

mcqs.question: Consider the following Statement: “The data set will contain an end of file character.”What characteristic of SRS is being depicted here ?
mcqs.explanation: An SRS is unambiguous if and only if, every requirement stated therein has only one unique interpretation. The given statement does not answer the question: “which data set will have an end of file character ?”.

mcqs.question: Consider the following Statement: “The product should have a good human interface.”What characteristic of SRS is being depicted here ?
mcqs.explanation: An SRS is verifiable, if and only if, every requirement stated therein is verifiable. The statement can only be answered on completion of the software and customer evaluation but still human interface will vary from person to person.

mcqs.question: Narrative essay is one of the best types of specification document ?
mcqs.explanation: Narrative essay is one of the worst types of specification document as it is difficult to change, difficult to be precise, has scope for contradictions, etc.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Requirement Management
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Requirement Management”.

mcqs.question: Which two requirements are given priority during Requirement Management of a product ?
mcqs.explanation: Enduring requirements are core requirements & are related to main activity of the organization while volatile requirements are likely to change during software development life cycle or after delivery of the product.

mcqs.question: Considering the example of issue/return of a book, cataloging etc. in a library management.What type of management requirement is being depicted here?
mcqs.explanation: For library management system issue/return of a book, cataloging etc. are core activities and are stable for any system.

mcqs.question: Why is Requirements Management Important ? It is due to the changes

options.d: d) in all of the mentioned.

mcqs.answer: d) in all of the mentioned.
mcqs.explanation: Systems continue to be built as the advancement of new products being launched in the market and so does the market changes, the technology and in turn customer’s expectation.

mcqs.question: Requirements Management is a prerequisite for Quality-Oriented Development.
mcqs.explanation: Quality makes no sense without reference to requirements, which means quality-oriented development is requirements-driven development, thus requirements management is a prerequisite for quality-oriented development.

mcqs.question: Requirements traceability is one of the most important part requirement management. It may also be referred to as the heart of requirement management.
mcqs.explanation: Requirements traceability refers to the ability to describe and follow the life of a requirement in both forwards and backwards direction. Requirements can be traced from its origins, through its development and specification, to its subsequent deployment and use, and through periods of ongoing refinement and iteration in any of these phases.

mcqs.question: Requirements Management has a high initial start-up cost but does not need ongoing funding throughout a project.
mcqs.explanation: Requirements Management needs continued funding throughout a project.Project funding is often limited at the onset of a project, restricted to those aspects of the project which are tangible and visible, and subsequently allocated in a phase-by-phase manner.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a Requirement Management workbench tool ?
mcqs.explanation: Rational Suite is an environment tool for requirement management.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a requirement management activity ?
mcqs.explanation: All the options are the activities of requirement management.

mcqs.question: What functionality of Requirement Management Tool (RMT) is depicted by the statement: “the tool should be able to automatically detect relations between artifacts. For example information retrieval techniques, monitoring of change history, naming schemas or model transformations.”

options.d: d) Automatic Link Creation and Change

mcqs.explanation: DOORS is one such tool that supports Automatic Link Detection.

mcqs.question: According to a statistical report: “over 30% of all software projects are cancelled before completion and over 70% of the remainder fail to deliver expected features”. What must be the reason for such a situation ?
mcqs.explanation: Fundamental to the problem mentioned in the statistical report is poor requirements management. Option a and c are its sub parts.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: System Modelling – 1
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “System Modelling – 1”.

mcqs.question: The Unified Modeling Language (UML) has become an effective standard for software modelling.How many different notations does it have ?
mcqs.explanation: The different notations of UML includes the nine UML diagrams namely class, object, sequence, collaboration, activity, state-chart, component, deployment and use case diagrams.

mcqs.question: Which model in system modelling depicts the dynamic behaviour of the system ?
mcqs.explanation: Behavioral models are used to describe the dynamic behavior of an executing system. This can be modeled from the perspective of the data processed by the system or by the events that stimulate responses from a system.

mcqs.question: Which model in system modelling depicts the static nature of the system ?
mcqs.explanation: Structural models show the organization and architecture of a system. These are used to define the static structure of classes in a system and their associations.

mcqs.question: Which perspective in system modelling shows the system or data architecture.
mcqs.explanation: Structural perspective is used to define the static structure of classes in a system and their associations.

mcqs.question: Which system model is being depicted by the ATM operations shown below:
mcqs.explanation: Context models are used to illustrate the operational context of a system.They show what lies outside the system boundaries.

mcqs.question: Activity diagrams are used to model the processing of data.
mcqs.explanation: The statement mentioned is true and each activity represents one process step.

mcqs.question: Model-driven engineering is just a theoretical concept. It cannot be converted into a working/executable code.
mcqs.explanation: Model-driven engineering is an approach to software development in which a system is represented as a set of models that can be automatically transformed to executable code.

mcqs.question: The UML supports event-based modeling using ____________ diagrams.
mcqs.explanation: State diagrams show system states and events that cause transitions from one state to another.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: System Modelling – 2
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “System Modelling – 2”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following diagram is not supported by UML considering Data-driven modeling ?
mcqs.explanation: DFDs focus on system functions and do not recognize system objects.

mcqs.question: _________________ allows us to infer that different members of classes have some common characteristics.
mcqs.explanation: Generalization is an everyday technique that we use to manage complexity.This means that common information will be maintained in one place only.

mcqs.question: One creates Behavioral models of a system when you are discussing and designing the system architecture.
mcqs.explanation: Structural models of software display the organization of a system in terms of the components that make up that system and their relationships.

mcqs.question: ______________ & ______________ diagrams of UML represent Interaction modeling.
mcqs.explanation: Use case modeling is mostly used to model interactions between a system and external actors.Sequence diagrams are used to model interactions between system components, although external agents may also be included.

mcqs.question: Which level of Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) models all entities and relationships ?
mcqs.explanation: Level 1 ERD models all data objects (entities) and their “connections” to one another while Level 3 ERD models all entities, relationships, and the attributes that provide further depth. Thus option b is correct.

mcqs.question: ___________ classes are used to create the interface that the user sees and interacts with as the software is used.
mcqs.explanation: The answer is self-explanatory.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statement is incorrect regarding the Class-responsibility-collaborator (CRC) modeling ?

options.a: a) All use-case scenarios (and corresponding use-case diagrams) are organized into categories in CRC modelling
options.b: b) The review leader reads the use-case deliberately
options.c: c) Only developers in the review (of the CRC model) are given a subset of the CRC model index cards

mcqs.answer: c) Only developers in the review (of the CRC model) are given a subset of the CRC model index cards
mcqs.explanation: All participants in the review (of the CRC model) are given a subset of the CRC model index cards.

mcqs.question: A data object can encapsulates processes and operation as well.
mcqs.explanation: A data object encapsulates data only. There is no reference within a data object to operations that act on the data.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Software Evolution
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Software Evolution”.

mcqs.question: The two dimensions of spiral model are
mcqs.explanation: The radial dimension depicts the cumulative costs and the angular dimension depicts the progress made in completing each cycle. Each loop of the spiral model represents a phase.

mcqs.question: The Incremental Model is combination of elements of

options.a: a) Build & FIX Model & Waterfall Model

mcqs.explanation: Each linear sequence produces a deliverable “increment” of the software system, particularly needed in case of quick delivery of a limited functionality system..

mcqs.question: Model preferred to create client/server applications is
mcqs.explanation: In case of client/server applications, the concurrent process model specifies activities in two dimensions: a system dimension and a component dimension. Hence Concurrency is achieved by these two activities occurring simultaneously and can be modeled using the state-oriented approach.

mcqs.question: Identify the correct statement with respect to Evolutionary development:

options.a: a) Evolutionary development usually has two flavors; exploratory development, and throw-away prototyping
options.b: b) Very large projects are usually done using  evolutionary development based approach
options.c: c) It facilitates easy project management, through the high volume of documentation it generates
options.d: d) Sometimes the construction of a throw-away prototype is not followed by a re- implementation of the software system using a more structured approach

mcqs.answer: a) Evolutionary development usually has two flavors; exploratory development, and throw-away prototyping
mcqs.explanation:
Evolutionary development usually has two flavors; exploratory development, and
throw-away prototyping.

mcqs.question: Spiral model was developed by
mcqs.explanation: Berry Boehm in 1986 in his Article “A spiral model of software development and enhancement”.

mcqs.question: Software evolution does not comprises:
mcqs.explanation: Software evolution refers to the study and management of the process of making changes to software over time. Thus it comprises rest three options.

mcqs.question: Processes for evolving a software product depend on:

options.a: a) Type of software to be maintained
options.c: c) Skills and experience of the people involved

mcqs.explanation: Processes used for software evolution depend on all these factors.

mcqs.question: Which technique is applied to ensure the continued evolution of legacy systems ?
mcqs.explanation: Processes used for software evolution depend rely on these two techniques.

mcqs.question: Program modularization and Source code translation are the activities of_____________
mcqs.explanation: Reengineering is the examination and alteration of a subject system to reconstitute it in a new form and the subsequent implementation of the new form.

mcqs.question: Reverse engineering is the last activity in a reengineering project.
mcqs.explanation: Reverse engineering is often the initial activity in a reengineering project.

mcqs.question: The cost of re-engineering is often significantly less than the costs of developing new software.
mcqs.explanation: There is a high risk in new software development. There may be development problems, staffing problems and specification problems, thereby increasing the cost.

links.text: Software Engineering MCQ: Sociotechnical Systems
links.context: This set of Software Engineering Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Sociotechnical Systems”.

mcqs.question: A sociotechnical system is a system that includes
mcqs.explanation: A sociotechnical system is a system that includes people, software, and hardware to show that you need to take a systems perspective on security and dependability.

mcqs.question: Which layer is missing in the sociotechnical system stack as shown below:
mcqs.explanation:
The application layer This layer delivers the application-specific functionality
that is required.

mcqs.question: Consider an example of a system which has a police command and control system that may include a geographical information system to provide details of the location of incidents. What kind of system the example represents?

options.d: d) Both Complex and Sociotechnical System

mcqs.answer: d) Both Complex and Sociotechnical System
mcqs.explanation: Complex systems are usually hierarchical and so include other systems.

mcqs.question: Which property of a sociotechnical system varies depending on how the component assemblies are arranged and connected?
mcqs.explanation: The volume of a system (the total space occupied) varies depending on how the component assemblies are arranged and connected.

mcqs.question: Which property of a sociotechnical system depends on the technical system components, its operators, and its operating environment?
mcqs.explanation: Usability reflects how easy it is to use the system.

mcqs.question: In a sociotechnical system, you need to consider reliability from perspectives namely:

options.d: d) hardware, software and operator reliability

mcqs.answer: d) hardware, software and operator reliability
mcqs.explanation: In a sociotechnical system, you need to consider reliability from all three perspectives.

mcqs.question: There are ________ overlapping stages in the lifetime of large and complex sociotechnical systems.
mcqs.explanation: The stages are Procurement, Development and Operation.

mcqs.question: Sociotechnical systems are deterministic.

links.context: This set of Project Management Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) covers essential topics like risk management, scheduling, and stakeholder roles, helping you test and enhance your knowledge effectively.

mcqs.question: What is the primary goal of project management?

options.c: c) To ensure the project is the most innovative
options.d: d) To complete the project on time and within budget

mcqs.answer: d) To complete the project on time and within budget
mcqs.explanation: The primary goal of project management is to complete the project on time, within budget, and according to scope.

mcqs.question: What is a project scope?

options.b: b) The project’s goals and deliverables
options.c: c) The project’s risk management plan

mcqs.answer: b) The project’s goals and deliverables
mcqs.explanation: The project scope outlines the project’s goals, deliverables, and boundaries, guiding the team’s work.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a goal of project management?

options.b: b) Maintaining a happy and well-functioning development team
options.c: c) Delivering the software to the customer at the agreed time
options.d: d) Keeping overall costs within budget

mcqs.explanation: Projects need to be managed because professional software engineering is always subject to organizational budget and schedule constraints.

mcqs.question: Project managers have to assess the risks that may affect a project.
mcqs.explanation: Risk management involves anticipating risks that might affect the project schedule or the quality of the software being developed, and then taking action to avoid these risks.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not considered a risk in project management?
mcqs.explanation: Testing is a part of project, thus it can’t be categorized as risk.

mcqs.question: What is the term for the process that a project manager follows throughout the entire life of a project?
mcqs.explanation: The Project Management Life Cycle refers to the series of phases a project manager follows from initiation to completion, ensuring the project’s successful execution.

mcqs.question: How is a 66.6% probability of risk typically categorized?
mcqs.explanation: The probability of the risk might be assessed as very low (<10%), low (10–25%), moderate (25–50%), high (50–75%), or very high (>75%).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is/are main parameters that you should use when computing the costs of a software development project?

options.d: d) Effort costs (the costs of paying software engineers and managers)

mcqs.explanation: Estimation involves working out how much effort is required to complete each activity and, from this, calculating the total cost of activities.

mcqs.question: What is the focus of quality planning in project management?
mcqs.explanation: The quality plan should set out the desired software qualities and describe how these are to be assessed.

mcqs.question: What is the first step in the project management process?
mcqs.explanation: Initiating the project is the first step, where objectives, stakeholders, and feasibility are identified to set the groundwork for planning.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect activity for the configuration management of a software system?
mcqs.explanation: Configuration management policies and processes define how to record and process proposed system changes, how to decide what system components to change, how to manage different versions of the system and its components, and how to distribute changes to customers.

mcqs.question: Which sub-process is part of process improvement?
mcqs.explanation: The current process is assessed, and process weaknesses and bottlenecks are identified.

mcqs.question: An independent relationship must exist between the attribute that can be measured and the external quality attribute.
mcqs.explanation: The value of the quality attribute must be related, in some way, to the value of the attribute than can be measured.

mcqs.question: What is a Gantt chart used for in project management?

options.d: d) Scheduling tasks and tracking progress

mcqs.answer: d) Scheduling tasks and tracking progress
mcqs.explanation: A Gantt chart visually represents the project timeline, showing the start and finish of tasks and their dependencies.

mcqs.question: Which method focuses on delivering work in short iterations and continuous improvement?
mcqs.explanation: The Agile method delivers work in iterations, ensuring adaptability and continuous feedback.

mcqs.question: What is risk management in project management?

options.a: a) The process of identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks
options.b: b) The process of training team members
options.c: c) The process of increasing the project budget
options.d: d) The process of controlling project scope changes

mcqs.answer: a) The process of identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks
mcqs.explanation: Risk management involves identifying, analyzing, and taking steps to reduce or control potential risks that may affect the project.

mcqs.question: Why is communication important in project management?

options.b: b) To ensure transparency and collaboration among stakeholders

mcqs.answer: b) To ensure transparency and collaboration among stakeholders
mcqs.explanation: Effective communication fosters collaboration, transparency, and a clear understanding of project goals among stakeholders.

mcqs.question: What is a project stakeholder?

options.a: a) A person or group that has an interest in the project’s outcome
options.b: b) A person responsible for executing tasks
options.c: c) A person who evaluates the project’s performance
options.d: d) A person who funds the project

mcqs.answer: a) A person or group that has an interest in the project’s outcome
mcqs.explanation: A stakeholder is anyone who has an interest in or is affected by the project’s outcomes, such as team members, clients, and sponsors.

mcqs.question: What is the purpose of a Project Manager’s role?

options.a: a) To work only on the planning phase
options.b: b) To oversee the project’s progress and deliver results
options.c: c) To handle technical tasks only

mcqs.answer: b) To oversee the project’s progress and deliver results
mcqs.explanation: A Project Manager oversees progress, coordinates resources, and ensures project deliverables are met according to plan.

options.d: d) The end results or outputs of the project

mcqs.answer: d) The end results or outputs of the project
mcqs.explanation: Deliverables are the specific results or outputs that must be produced to complete the project.

mcqs.question: What is the purpose of the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)?

options.a: a) To only focus on deadlines
options.c: c) To break down project work into manageable tasks

mcqs.answer: c) To break down project work into manageable tasks
mcqs.explanation: A WBS breaks a project into smaller, manageable parts, ensuring every detail is planned and executed.

options.b: b) Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
options.c: c) Sustainable, Measurable, Agile, Reliable, Timely
options.d: d) Systematic, Measurable, Achievable, Risk-free, Timely

mcqs.answer: b) Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
mcqs.explanation: SMART goals are defined as Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound to ensure clarity and focus.

mcqs.question: Which document includes the project timeline, milestones, and deliverables?

options.a: a) Allocating, monitoring, and controlling costs

mcqs.answer: a) Allocating, monitoring, and controlling costs
mcqs.explanation: Budget Management allocates, monitors, and controls project costs to ensure financial resources are effectively utilized.

mcqs.explanation: A Project Sponsor provides funding, support, and high-level strategic guidance for the project’s success.

mcqs.explanation: The PERT technique estimates task durations and dependencies, ensuring accurate project planning.
